precepts.text: But I thought the scripture says in a multitude of counsel there's safety. That seems to be the total opposite of what the Bible tells us.
precepts.point: So it says, and let the counsel of your own heart stand. There's no man more faithful unto thee. But I thought the scripture says in a multitude of counsel there's safety. That seems to be the total opposite of what the Bible tells us. Should we not seek counsel? Only a few people know that. Okay, wait a second. Do you all understand that in a multitude of counsel there's safety? What does that mean? In a multitude of counsel there's safety. Who can help me out understand that? Okay. Right there. Keep on, right to the back. Right there. Stand up.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
Sirach says, “And let the counsel of thine own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful unto thee than it.” But the scripture also says, “Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.” At first that seems to be the total opposite. Should we not seek counsel?

In the multitude of counsellors there is safety means that as much counsel as you can get will help you make the right decisions and move in the right direction. That is correct. And the counsel of your own heart can stand only when it is funnelled through the laws of God, through the scriptures. Then you can make your decision and stand on it, because it is based on the laws of God.

Go up to verse 12 and it opens: “But be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord.” Your everyday life should be spent around godly people, and if you lack understanding, around people with more understanding than you, so you can level up. You know who keeps the commandments by being exercised to discern between good and evil, and every beast consorts with its own kind. Such a man “will sorrow with thee, if thou shalt miscarry”: he will correct you.

So letting the counsel of your own heart stand is not for the man who seeks no counsel and makes his decisions while watching porn. He is going to make a mistake. It is for the man whose mind is godly, like the godly man he took counsel from. “For a man’s mind is sometime wont to tell him more than seven watchmen, that sit above in an high tower.”

“And above all this pray to the most High, that he will direct thy way in truth.” Above your own heart and above the counsel of a friend, you go to God, and God does not hear the prayer of sinners. “Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” So the two scriptures agree: get counsel from the brothers, balance it with what you think is right with a godly mind, then ask God to direct your path.

precepts.text: But God is not going to hear the prayer of sinners, right?
precepts.point: But listen, then you pray to God. But God is not going to hear the prayer of sinners, right? So it say above the counsel of your own heart, above the counsel of a friend, you go to God and he's going to direct your path. Look what it says next.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
“But be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord.” Your everyday life should generally be spent around godly people. We have to go out in the world and work, but outside of that, the bulk of your time is with godly men, and if the brothers around you don't have understanding, be around people with more understanding than you so you can level up. How will you know he keeps the commandments? You have to be exercised to discern between good and evil. If you are keeping the commandments, you'll be around godly men, because every beast consorteth with its own kind.

He is one whose mind is according to thy mind, “and will sorrow with thee, if thou shalt miscarry”: he's going to correct you. So how is your mind? It has to be godly. When it says “let the counsel of thine own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful unto thee than it”, that is not for the man who isn't seeking counsel, who is watching porn, whatever he's doing, and then making decisions. You're going to make a mistake. In a multitude of counsel there is safety; the counsel of your own heart stands when it's funneled through the laws of God. “For a man’s mind is sometime wont to tell him more than seven watchmen, that sit above in an high tower”: the seven watchmen are godly men, and your own godly mind can see what's best for you.

“And above all this pray to the most High, that he will direct thy way in truth.” Above the counsel of your own heart, above the counsel of a godly man, you go to God, and he directs your path. But God is not going to hear the prayer of sinners: “If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me.” Your prayer for direction is only heard if your heart is not holding on to iniquity.

“Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” So it's not telling you not to get counsel from brothers. Get counsel, balance it with what you think might be right, with a godly mind, and then go to God and ask him to direct your path.

precepts.text: There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself. That is what Eliphaz was telling Job: you were the guy that comforted everybody, but now that your turn has come, you are fainting and want to give up. We should all be mindful of that.
precepts.point: But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest: now judgment has come upon you, Job, and now you have given up, you have lost the spirit. Where is that mighty man that helped all the people?

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
Eliphaz the Temanite, one of Job's friends, tells him, “Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.” You were the one that strengthened men and women when they were weak; your words upheld those that fell down in grief and in sin. “But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.” Now judgment has come upon you, Job, and now you have given up, you have lost the spirit. Where is that mighty man that helped all the people? Now you're upset, your lips stuck out, you got an attitude.

Sirach says it plainly, and it is something we should all be mindful of: “There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself.” That is what Eliphaz was telling Job. You were the guy that comforted everybody, but now that your turn has come, now that judgment has come upon you, you are fainting and want to give up.

And Job had been that man. He remembered the days “When his candle shined upon my head, and when by his light I walked through darkness”: the commandment is a lamp and the law is light. He was a judge who sat in the gate; young men hid themselves and the aged stood up when he came. “I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.” He knew what to say to the dying and “caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.” “I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame. I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out.”

That is how Job represents the twelve tribes. What Job went through, we go through as a nation of people, because we were the servants of God, and when the trials came, we gave up, gave in to sin and turned our back on the Lord. The one who taught many has to be profitable to himself when his own trial comes.

precepts.text: Every friend saith, I am his friend also: but there is a friend, which is only a friend in name. Is it not a grief unto death, when a companion and friend is turned to an enemy? There is a companion which rejoiceth in the prosperity of a friend, but in the time of trouble will be against him. They had one dispute, and he ran to the other nations and told them about all the money in Jerusalem.
precepts.point: And when he could not overcome Onias, he got him to Apollonius the governor of Coelosyria and Phenice. He ran to the other nations. They were working together on this temple, and because of one argument he goes to the other nations against Onias, and told them that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of infinite sums of money. You cannot make this stuff up.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
Simon fell out with Onias, and “when he could not overcome Onias”, he went to Apollonius, the governor of Celosyria and Phenice, and “told him that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of infinite sums of money.” They were working together on the temple; they had one dispute; Onias as high priest had the last say, and Simon did not agree. So he ran to the other nations against him. You can't make this stuff up.

Sirach describes that man: “Every friend saith, I am his friend also: but there is a friend, which is only a friend in name. Is it not a grief unto death, when a companion and friend is turned to an enemy? O wicked imagination, whence camest thou in to cover the earth with deceit? There is a companion, which rejoiceth in the prosperity of a friend, but in the time of trouble will be against him.”

That is Simon: a friend only in name, a companion turned into an enemy. Because of one argument, he told the heathen about all the money in Jerusalem.

And that money was not his to give away. The treasury held what the law set aside: the tithe for the Levites, who had no inheritance, and for the stranger, the fatherless and the widow, so that the Lord might bless the work of their hands. So he was ready to see the Greeks take what belonged to the widows and orphans rather than let Onias have the last word. This is a no good dude: from brother to betrayer.

precepts.text: There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself. When difficult situations come, he does not apply anything he has been teaching. That is called a hypocrite. You can only find that out when he or she is in a difficult situation, whether it is covetousness, stealing, adultery, or hatred.
precepts.point: All the men in the scriptures that set order and structure were disliked: Jeremiah, Ezekiel, the apostles, Paul, Samuel, Christ. If you are a man about structure, order, and discipline in your household, you are going to be the least liked. But if you are a man of the truth, you do not care; your job is to structure and order. Men, your job is to raise up the 144,000.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Part of assessing a man for order is integrity: his actions in private compared to his words. “There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself.” He teaches many, but when difficult situations come, he does not apply anything he has been teaching.

That is called a hypocrite. And you can only find it out when he or she is in a difficult situation, whether it is covetousness, stealing, adultery or hatred. That is why the assessment looks at how a man lives, not only how he talks: his honesty, his responsibility, his family, his finances, how he handles conflict.

A man set in authority has to profit himself with what he teaches. Paul joyed in beholding their order and the stedfastness of their faith; a teacher who is unprofitable to himself does not fit the bill, however much he knows.

precepts.text: Let reason go before every enterprise and counsel before every action: get counsel before you seal the deal, and save yourself a whole lot of heartache.
precepts.point: Extol not thyself in the counsel of thine own heart, lest thy soul be torn in pieces as a bull straying alone and thou be left as a dry tree: so many have fallen victim to their own counsel, driving the wrong way up the highway while the officer says turn around.

note.label: Why Do Fools Fall In Love

precepts.why:
Sirach warns, “Extol not thyself in the counsel of thine own heart; that thy soul be not torn in pieces as a bull straying alone.” That forward thinking, not looking for counsel, not trying to seek or find out, has destroyed so many people. So many have fallen victim to their own counsel and their own mind, thinking they have it figured out. You don’t got the answers, sway. The direction you are heading is the wrong way. Imagine driving on the wrong side of the highway with the officer telling you, turn around, and you say he doesn’t know what he’s talking about. Boom, you dead.

The remedy is Sirach 37: “Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” Before every enterprise, make sure it is sound, that it makes sense, that thought has been put into it. Never do anything on a whim, piecing things together with half-assed research.

“And counsel before every action.” Before you make a move, before you seal the deal, get counsel and find out if this is what you should do, and you will save yourself a whole lot of heartache.

Nobody in this camp has an excuse to say there is no one to talk to. There are men here who have gone through it and senior sisters who have dealt with it, who can help you make the right decision in a proving if you are honest and open about what you are experiencing. They can help you see the red flags, and also the things in yourself you may not see, so you can conquer them and continue the proving process instead of being left “as a dry tree.”

precepts.text: A captain's precept. There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself. Leaders in the other camps know the laws but their god is money or power over the people, so they are unprofitable to themselves, and nothing will stay hid.
precepts.point: Let the sisters get counsel from sisters. When you do give counsel, it must be what God wants them to hear and beneficial to them, not to your own wants.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
“There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself.” You cannot be a hypocrite, especially in a leadership position. Look at the other camps: they are supposed to be leading the people, but their mind is on the riches, or on how many bodies they can put as a notch in their belt.

There is one that is supposed to be wise. What makes you wise? Keeping the commandments. Those leaders know that. They know they are Israel, they know they are God's chosen people, and they know they are supposed to be keeping the laws. Yet because of their bad intentions and covetousness, because their god is money, or their god is power to move and persuade the people, they are unprofitable to themselves.

And nothing will be hid. Everything that is done will be revealed in time. That is the other side of Deuteronomy 7: the Lord “keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations; And repayeth them that hate him to their face, to destroy them”. If you use a position to lead and teach the people and then take advantage of them, beguiling the sisters into sex, keeping them in a filthy mindset, or taking their money, God will judge you. You hate God and you hate his people.

precepts.text: My son, prove thy soul and thy life, and see what is evil for it, and give not that unto it; for all things are not profitable for all men, neither hath every soul pleasure in every thing. Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing, nor too greedy upon meats, for excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler. It is literally about food, and spiritually about proving your spirit: see what is evil for you and give it not, whether a food or a show like Spartacus full of sex scenes. A fat brother's diet is different from a slim officer's.
precepts.point: The Lord is using Captain Shem's initiative with the yellow and red brothers for your health, because we need brothers fit and in the street to teach. Knowing it is not good for you and still indulging shows you lack discipline; a man who cannot control his own thoughts accomplishes nothing.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
“Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee.” We usually use flee for lust, but you cannot flee from something that is in your refrigerator or your freezer. The brain does not distinguish: the same dopamine and reward centers fire for food that pleases the flesh as for sex. Flee from the unhealthy foods, or they bite you and destroy you. That is why so many brothers have health issues, in the hospital every week and unable to make the Sabbath. You need a healthy vessel to do the work.

Sirach goes further: “My son, prove thy soul in thy life, and see what is evil for it, and give not that unto it.” From verse 27 down to 30 it is literally about food, and spiritually it is about proving your spirit. Just as you see which foods make you sick and unhealthy, see what things are evil for you and make you mentally unhealthy, and give not that unto it. Spartacus was a good show, with a whole lot of sex scenes; you may have to say, I can’t watch this.

“For all things are not profitable for all men, neither hath every soul pleasure in every thing.” A fat brother’s diet is different from a slim officer’s. “Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing, nor too greedy upon meats: For excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler.” Don’t overindulge beyond your limits, and don’t eat excessively.

Food porn works on the brain the same way pornography does, because the brain sees both as nourishment. There is a healthy pleasure and an unhealthy one: healthy food instead of junk, your wife instead of the screen. Peter says, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul. When you are counting calories and a 240-calorie cookie calls you with 100 left, you feel that war inside. It is the same temptation, a worldly lust we inherited through America.

“By surfeiting have many perished; but he that taketh heed prolongeth his life.” The Lord is putting us on another level of discipline, because we need brothers fit and in the street teaching.

precepts.text: Let reason go before every enterprise, and counsel before every action. Apply the counsel and things go well.
precepts.point: Once a man has a little money he feels grown and asks who anyone is to counsel him. Months or years later, when everything falls apart, then he wants counsel. It is needed before, not after.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

precepts.why:
“Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.” Why? Because of what you were supposed to do first: “Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” Everything you take on to do, you are supposed to seek counsel. And if you seek counsel and apply it, things are going to go well for you.

But instead of seeking counsel, pride kicks in. I am my own man, I do what I want. A lot of times when brothers have bad dealings with each other, both of them were out of the spirit, because neither one ever asked for counsel: Listen, I want to do this job with so-and-so; what do you think about it?

Once people have a little money in their pocket, they feel grown. I own my own house, I bought it with my own money, I am doing better than you; who are you to counsel me? Then months later, years later, when everything falls apart, now they want counsel. Counsel did not go before that enterprise; pride went before it, and destruction came with it.

You need counsel before, not after. That is why we have to remember the scriptures: blessed is he that readeth, and if we apply what we read, we are going to be all right. Reason and counsel before every action is the cure for the pride that goes before destruction.

precepts.text: He that sinneth before his Maker, let him fall into the hand of the physician.
precepts.point: Calling this bullying means refusing to take heed, and that brings a short life. That is the Bible's word, not the teacher's.

note.label: My Temple My Choice

precepts.why:
“For excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler.” That belly ache late at night, that belly pain: you are sick. “By surfeiting have many perished; but he that taketh heed prolongeth his life.” The Bible says if you keep overeating, you are going to die. So I guess the Bible is a bully’s book? No. You just hate God and you hate yourself, because loving God is the only way to love yourself. When the white man’s own Department of Health says eight Swedish fish is past a child’s safe arsenic level, you say nothing; when we tell you to stop eating junk, it’s bullying. If you call it bullying, you will not take heed, and you will live a very short life. That is what the Bible says, not what I say.

Then Sirach says: “He that sinneth before his Maker, let him fall into the hand of the physician.” What will make you get sick and fall into the hand of the physician? Overeating. The Bible says, if you want to live long, don’t do it. But do we take heed? No, we don’t.

Fat does not stay harmlessly under the skin. Visceral fat wraps around the heart, the lungs, the liver, the stomach and the intestines, and makes your organs work double time, so you always feel weak, tired, low on energy. You don’t feel pain, so you don’t think it’s happening, until one day, bam, stroke; bam, heart attack; high cholesterol, heart bypass surgery. Eating sugar and overeating, you walk around like a ticking time bomb.

That is what we are trying to prevent: you ending up in a hospital bed, in the physician’s hand, because you sinned against your Maker with your mouth. Take heed to what is written, and prolong your life.

precepts.text: Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing nor too greedy upon meats; excess of meats bringeth sickness.
precepts.point: Fish is meat; all flesh is not the same flesh, but the flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are all flesh. Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God, and the word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
“Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you” is the introduction of man eating meat. The Most High did not give man a new stomach; the body was already made for it and it lay dormant until after the flood.

Having the liberty to eat meat does not mean eating without balance. “My son, prove thy soul in thy life, and see what is evil for it, and give not that unto it. For all things are not profitable for all men, neither hath every soul pleasure in every thing.” “Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing, nor too greedy upon meats: For excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler. By surfeiting have many perished; but he that taketh heed prolongeth his life.”

precepts.text: Be not too greedy upon meats, for excess of meats bringeth sickness, and by surfeiting many have perished.
precepts.point: The Most High had overfed them because they murmured, but the lesson also stands in nature: excess of meat brings sickness. Animal protein is good for the body, but it is a matter of moderation, not overindulgence.

note.label: Numbers 11: Beware of Murmuring

precepts.why:
The Lord gave them quails two cubits high round about the camp, and “while the flesh was yet between their teeth, ere it was chewed, the wrath of the Lord was kindled against the people, and the Lord smote the people with a very great plague”, exactly as He had warned. The Most High had overfed them because they murmured, and the place was called Kibrothhattaavah, the graves of lust, “because there they buried the people that lusted.”

The lesson also stands in nature. “Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing, nor too greedy upon meats: For excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler. By surfeiting have many perished; but he that taketh heed prolongeth his life.”

Animal protein is good for the body, but it is a matter of moderation, not overindulgence. Excess of meat brings sickness, and by surfeiting many have perished, as they perished at the graves of lust.

precepts.text: Counsel before every action; that is what our forefathers did not do here.
precepts.point: This type of ordeal will play out again in the times when Christ returns: the sons of strangers shall come to build up Israel's walls, their kings shall minister unto Israel, and the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish. There is nothing new under the sun.

note.label: Joshua 9: The Gibeonite Deception and the Weight of an Oath

precepts.why:
“And the men took of their victuals, and asked not counsel at the mouth of the Lord.” That is the first mistake. “Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” Let reason think on whether it is the right move, and even before you reason within yourself, the Most High says counsel, counsel, counsel before every action.

Our forefathers did not do that here, and not asking counsel of the Most High at this moment ended up being a snare and a trap to us as a people, as the rest of the scriptures show.

points: My son, prove thy soul in thy life, and see what is evil for it, and give not that unto it. This part of the chapter goes into various things that you may deem to be good for you but that are not really good for you. It goes into different types of food, down in verse 29 it goes into dainties and so forth. But though contextually it goes into those various things like overeating, that short part of the verse covers everything.

You have to examine what is evil for your life and abstain from it. It is not only food. It is also the company you keep. It is also the things that you watch, the things that you entertain and give ear to. All of these things you have to examine. What is going to cause me to risk it all, and is it worthy for me to lose it all because of what my soul or spirit desires, or what my flesh lusts after? Am I willing to lose it all for this?

And give not that unto it. Do not give yourself over to it. You have to prove your life. I remember Bishop did a class about taking moral inventory. You take moral inventory. See what is evil for you and do not give yourself over to it.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: For all things are not profitable for all men, neither hath every soul pleasure in every thing. So what may be good for one brother is definitely not good for another. What is good for one sister is definitely not good for another sister. So you have to know yourself, to see what is beneficial or detrimental for your life.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself. So King David a prophet of God, King Saul chosen of God, but at that particular moment for King Saul, he was unprofitable to himself until the repentant process came in, because he committed the transgressions. That is just like all of us.

You do not want to be the one who has the wisdom of the Lord, and he called you with that wisdom, and yet is unprofitable to himself. Due to your lack of application, or examining yourself, you are unprofitable to yourself. You were beneficial to everybody else. Everyone that came your way, you were able to answer questions. You cast down imaginations. Anything that exalted itself against the knowledge of God, you were casting everything down. But now, when it is time for you to apply, there is an issue.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: My son, prove thy soul in thy life, and see what is evil for it, and give not that unto it. Prove what your soul want and prove what is evil for it, the things that you should not be eating or consuming.

note.label: FDA: Food And Drug Assassination

points: For all things are not profitable for all men: everybody can't eat everything. Some people eat chocolate and they break out. Me, I love chocolate, but I try not to eat it too much; I cut it down to once a month now.
Neither hath every soul pleasure in every thing: everybody don't like the same things.

note.label: FDA: Food And Drug Assassination

points: Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing: like sweets, don't be unsatiable, meaning you eat a lot of sweets. Now Esau is coming out: oh, sugar, too much sugar give you cancer. God tell us not to eat too much sugar, because he know what it does to your body. Now the white man is saying it, now you want to slow down.

Nor too greedy upon meat: don't eat too much meat. God says not to eat too much meat. We not supposed to be eating meat every day. For excess of meats bringeth sickness: so you going to get sick if you keep eating beef and chicken every day. That's what God says. Y'all could take it or leave it.

note.label: FDA: Food And Drug Assassination

points: And surfeiting will turn into choler: surfeiting meaning excess going to turn into choler, meaning to sickness.

note.label: FDA: Food And Drug Assassination

points: By surfeiting have many perished: by excess, many people perish. You eat too much sweets, you eat too much meat, now you sick and you died. So the Lord tell us how to deal with even food; he says not to have it in excess.

But he that taketh heed prolongeth his life: you're going to live longer. You're not going to die from colon cancer, you're not going to get diabetes by eating too much sugar. You're going to prolong your life if you take heed. Back then our forefathers understood these things, and we live long and we live healthy. Too much of nothing is good for you.

note.label: FDA: Food And Drug Assassination

points: Be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord. Not a man that appears to be godly, but one you know keeps the laws of God; and if you are tethered to wisdom, you will have a discerning spirit to know that. Whose mind is according to thy mind: your mind has to be a godly mind too; can two walk together except they be agreed? And he will sorrow with thee if thou shalt miscarry: a godly man fights with you to help you. I have to see the fight in you; if I see no fight, I wash my hands with a clear conscience.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

points: And let the counsel of thine own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful unto thee than it. Nobody is more faithful to you than your own mind; but if you are not a godly man, your thought process is corrupted, and your decisions will not be made right. Do not come to counsel with your mind already made up; you waste everybody's time.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

points: For a man's mind is sometime wont to tell him more than seven watchmen that sit above in an high tower. The watchmen see from a vantage point; you see your own life from ground level. A brother's counsel may be good from where he sits and still not fit what you are walking through, and brothers can be overbearing with counsel. So hear it from a neutral place.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

points: And above all this pray to the Most High, that he will direct thy way in truth. You listen to the counsel, you process it, then you go to God, and God will direct your way. Let reason go before every enterprise, and counsel before every action.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

points: My son, prove thy soul in thy life, and see what is evil for it, and give not that unto it. It is your temple and your choice, so choose what is good for it.
All things are not profitable for all men. No kind of man is made healthy by sugar.
Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing. Any means any: the candy bar with coconut or peanuts is still a dainty.

note.label: My Temple My Choice

points: Excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler. By surfeiting have many perished, but he that taketh heed prolongeth his life.
Calling this bullying means refusing to take heed, and that brings a short life. That is the Bible's word, not the teacher's.

note.label: My Temple My Choice

points: Some men act like they are doing you a good deed with counsel, and they are counselling for themselves.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

points: He tells you your way is good, then steps to the side to see what befalls you. When you get blasted he never said a thing.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

points: Number two: surround yourself with people who believe in you.
But be continually with a godly man. The Bible tells us to be continually with godly men.
Whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord. And that is how we identify the godly men, or the godly women: they keep the commandments of God.

Whose mind is according to thy mind. If my mind is to meditate therein day and night, to read my four chapters, to have a spirit of confidence, now I am going to be surrounded by other men that are confident too.

And will sorrow with thee, if thou shalt miscarry. Now, misery loves company. That is not what the Bible is telling us. So if I am dealing with a godly man that keeps the commandments, which breeds confidence in me and in him, when I fall on hard times, how is he going to sorrow with me? He is going to build me up. My brother will help build me up in my time of sorrow. And those are the type of people that we need to be surrounded by. Brothers that build you up, brothers that believe in you.
